query: Research the evidence on whether pair programming improves code quality. Synthesise the key findings, note where sources agree and disagree, and give a weighted verdict.
expected_behavior: Produces a structured synthesis with: (1) Source landscape - identifies primary research types: controlled studies (Williams et al.), industrial surveys, and practitioner reports; notes that most rigorous studies are small N (< 50 developers). (2) Agreement points - faster defect detection during writing (not review), knowledge transfer and bus-factor reduction, improved design discussion. (3) Disagreement points - productivity: studies show -15% to +40% depending on task complexity and pair experience; some find no effect on final defect rates after accounting for extra review time; remote pairing outcomes diverge sharply from co-located. (4) Confounders - task type (algorithmic vs. integration matters a lot), pair compatibility, junior/senior pairing vs same-level. (5) Weighted verdict - conditional support: pair programming likely positive for complex, high-risk code and onboarding; unclear for routine CRUD; cost-benefit depends on defect cost in the domain. Cites specific claims with source qualifiers ('Williams (2000) found...' not 'studies show').

query: I have three conflicting claims about LLM context window utilisation: (A) 'Models lose coherence after 50% context fill', (B) 'Performance degrades only past 80% fill', (C) 'It depends entirely on the task type'. Triangulate these.
expected_behavior: Applies a competing-hypothesis triangulation: (1) Identifies what each claim implies about the mechanism - A implies absolute position encoding limits, B implies softer attention dilution, C implies task-specific retrieval requirements. (2) Evidence that discriminates - needle-in-haystack benchmarks (e.g. RULER, Passkey Retrieval) show performance cliffs at different fill levels per model architecture; retrieval tasks degrade earlier than generation tasks. (3) Reconciliation - all three claims can be simultaneously true at different granularity: C is the meta-claim (task dependency), A and B describe the tails of the distribution for retrieval-heavy vs. generation-heavy tasks respectively. (4) Practical verdict - for retrieval-dependent tasks (RAG, long-doc QA), treat 50% as a conservative ceiling; for generation tasks (summarisation, continuation), 80% is more appropriate. Flags that this is model-architecture-specific and recommends empirical measurement over relying on benchmarks.

query: Synthesise internal post-mortem patterns: we've had 12 incidents in 6 months. Common themes I've noticed: 3 involved deploy-time config errors, 4 were downstream API timeouts, 3 were database connection pool exhaustion, 2 were unrelated. What systemic fixes should we prioritise?
expected_behavior: Produces a prioritised systemic analysis: (1) Pattern grouping - config errors (25%), downstream timeout (33%), connection pool exhaustion (25%), other (17%). The two most addressable clusters account for 58% of incidents. (2) Root cause per cluster - config errors: likely missing config validation in deploy pipeline or no pre-deploy smoke test; downstream timeouts: missing circuit breakers or timeout budgets propagating through service calls; connection pool exhaustion: pool sizing not tuned to traffic, missing pool monitoring/alerting. (3) Systemic fixes ranked by expected incident reduction: Circuit breaker pattern on all downstream calls (targets 4 incidents = 33%), connection pool monitoring + alerts + tuned sizing (targets 3 incidents = 25%), deploy-time config validation gate (targets 3 incidents = 25%). (4) Leading indicators to add: pool utilisation metric, downstream p99 latency trending, config diff in deploy PR template. Recommends fixing circuit breakers first as highest-impact, lowest-effort for distributed systems.
